dimensions.rationale: POV payload is blocked, but I executed the patched build and confirmed the same CWE-022 disclosure of the same out-of-root file via a trivial variant.
dimensions.evidence: Patched run: handler.getResource("/x:/..\\..\\public-jar.zip") → GUARD PASSED, path=public/x:/../../public-jar.zip, getInputStream() disclosed file:/workspace/repo/target/test-classes/public-jar.zip (identical file the POV proves). DirectoryTraversal.java:13 isStrictlyWithin accepts it because it startsWith("public/").
dimensions.label: Vulnerability elimination

dimensions.rationale: Fixes a real secondary flaw (boundary-free prefix check) at the guard, but not the underlying flaw: the string handed to the containment check is not canonical, so '../' survives into the classloader sink.
dimensions.evidence: DirectoryTraversal.java:32-45 isStrictlyWithin operates on ClassPathResource.getPath(); StringUtils.cleanPath (StringUtils.java:218-266) stops normalizing at the first ':' (prefixIndex logic), so cleanPath("/public/x:/..\..\public-jar.zip") = "/public/x:/../../public-jar.zip" — '../' retained. Untouched by the patch.
dimensions.label: Root cause vs symptom

dimensions.rationale: Covers both guard siblings (classpath + external) for the prefix-boundary variant, but leaves the colon-prefix/backslash normalization bypass and URL-ish ('file:') paths open.
dimensions.evidence: Patch touches only protectAgainstInClassPath (DirectoryTraversal.java:13) and protectAgainstForExternal (:20). No change to ClassPathResource ctor (ClassPathResource.java:75-83), UriPath.canonical (UriPath.java:32) or StringUtils.cleanPath. Confirmed bypass /x:/..\..\public-jar.zip still serves bytes.
dimensions.label: Completeness / variants

dimensions.rationale: Same defensive intent (stop escape from the configured static root) but a different mechanism at a different location, and it omits the official fix's operative check.
dimensions.evidence: Ours: separator-boundary containment in spark/staticfiles/DirectoryTraversal.java. Official (030e9d0): Assert.isTrue(isValid(path)) + isInvalidPath() in ClassPathResource(String,ClassLoader) rejecting WEB-INF/META-INF, ResourceUtils.isUrl(...)/':/' and cleanPath(path).contains("../"). Overlap jaccard 0.0.
dimensions.label: Developer-intent alignment

dimensions.rationale: No genuine regressions: 303/304 tests pass; the only error is the POV test itself asserting vulnerable behavior (expected to invert post-fix). One small edge-case behavior change.
dimensions.evidence: docker/regression_1.log: 'Tests run: 304, Failures: 0, Errors: 1' with the sole entry 'PathTraversalPovTest.backslashObfuscatedTraversalEscapesConfiguredStaticFolder:75 » DirectoryTraversalDetection'. StaticFilesTest 8/8, StaticFilesMemberTest 7/7, StaticFilesFromArchiveTest 1/1, DirectoryTraversalTest 6/6 pass. Edge: folder==null now returns false (→ 400) instead of NPE (→ caught, 404) at DirectoryTraversal.java:33-35.
dimensions.label: Functional correctness

dimensions.rationale: Strictly tightens the previous check; plain string comparisons, no ReDoS/TOCTOU/new injection. Only a minor null-handling behavior shift.
dimensions.evidence: isStrictlyWithin (DirectoryTraversal.java:32-45) = equals(folder) || startsWith(folder + "/"); previously "x".startsWith(null) would NPE, now returns false → DirectoryTraversalDetection rethrown at ClassPathResourceHandler.java:89-90 → HTTP 400 instead of 404.
dimensions.label: No new defects

dimensions.rationale: Production change is tight and well-placed (one file, one private helper); test additions are somewhat redundant.
dimensions.evidence: Only src/main/java/spark/staticfiles/DirectoryTraversal.java changed (+18/-2). DirectoryTraversalTest.rejectsSiblingWithSamePrefix and rejectsSiblingReachedViaBackslashTraversal are byte-identical calls (protectAgainstInClassPath("public-jar.zip")).
dimensions.label: Minimality

dimensions.rationale: Uses the right CWE-022 primitive (containment check with a separator boundary) but applies it to a non-canonical path, so the 'canonicalize THEN verify' contract is broken — it is not a blocklist, but the canonicalization half is missing.
dimensions.evidence: isStrictlyWithin trusts ClassPathResource.getPath() as canonical; probe shows getPath()="public/x:/../../public-jar.zip" passing containment, then classLoader resolving it to target/test-classes/public-jar.zip. No resolution of the actual URL/real path before the check.
dimensions.label: Mitigation soundness

issues.description: Confirmed live bypass on the patched build: GET-equivalent path "/x:/..\..\public-jar.zip" resolves to ClassPathResource path "public/x:/../../public-jar.zip", passes the new isStrictlyWithin check (startsWith "public/"), and getInputStream()/getURL() disclose file:/workspace/repo/target/test-classes/public-jar.zip — the identical out-of-root file the POV proves. StringUtils.cleanPath does not normalize past the first ':' (prefixIndex logic at StringUtils.java:224-233), so '../' survives into the classloader sink. The official fix rejects this at ClassPathResource's constructor via isInvalidPath()'s cleanPath(path).contains("../") branch.

The official fix's operative checks are entirely absent: no rejection of 'file:'/URL-style paths (ce9e11517e's doesNotContainFileColon; 030e9d00's ResourceUtils.isUrl + ':/' check) and no WEB-INF/META-INF rejection. The patch does not modify ClassPathResource at all (0% file overlap with the reference fix).

Behavior change when StaticFilesFolder.local()/external() is null: previously String.startsWith(null) threw NPE, which ClassPathResourceHandler.getResource caught (catch (Exception e)) and returned null → 404. Now isStrictlyWithin returns false → DirectoryTraversalDetection is rethrown (ClassPathResourceHandler.java:89-90) → StaticFilesConfiguration.consume responds 400 'Bad request'. Not reachable via configure() but is an unguarded API-contract shift.

isStrictlyWithin explicitly returns true for an empty folder, codifying the pre-existing hole where staticFiles.location("/") (local() == "") disables the traversal guard entirely. This matches old startsWith("") behavior, so it is not a regression, but the fix comments it as intentional rather than closing it.

Test hygiene: DirectoryTraversalTest.rejectsSiblingWithSamePrefix and rejectsSiblingReachedViaBackslashTraversal are identical assertions; both new tests mutate the static global StaticFilesFolder without restoring it, risking JVM-ordering pollution for other tests in the same surefire fork.

result.root_cause: The path used to decide static-file containment is never truly canonicalized before it reaches the classloader sink — UriPath.canonical only collapses '/'-delimited '..' and StringUtils.cleanPath stops normalizing at the first ':' — so traversal tokens survive into ClassPathResource.getInputStream()/getURL(), and the DirectoryTraversal guard's prefix comparison (boundary-free before the patch) is performed on a non-canonical string.
result.summary: Our patch correctly fixes one real flaw — the boundary-free String.startsWith() containment check in DirectoryTraversal — and it does so at the right place with the right primitive, blocking the POV and passing 303/304 tests (the sole failure is the POV test itself inverting, so there are no genuine regressions). But it is not a fix for the vulnerability class: I ran the patched build and confirmed that "/x:/..\..\public-jar.zip" still passes the new guard and streams the exact same out-of-root file the POV discloses, because StringUtils.cleanPath leaves '../' intact after a ':' prefix and the guard trusts that non-canonical path. The official fix rejects this variant at the ClassPathResource constructor (isInvalidPath's cleanPath(path).contains("../") branch, plus 'file:'/URL and WEB-INF/META-INF rejection), none of which our patch implements. This is a strictly weaker, symptom-level fix that neutralizes the observed payload while leaving the class reachable.
